previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A female patient with a complex medical history including end-stage renal disease, antiphospholipid syndrome, systemic lupus erythematosus, and seizure disorder was admitted for acute dizziness and transient difficulty speaking. Neurological evaluation ruled out stroke with normal imaging and a NIHSS score of zero, confirming peripheral vestibulopathy as the cause. She also presented with symptomatic bradycardia (heart rate 50) and hyperkalemia (potassium 7.0), both of which resolved after hemodialysis. Her symptoms improved significantly during the admission, with normalization of electrolytes and stable vital signs. She remained neurologically intact, ambulated independently, and was discharged home in stable condition with no medication changes except for a reduction in ranitidine dose. Follow-up was advised for ongoing management of anticoagulation, dialysis, and anemia.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ is a ___ y/o woman with a PMH of SLE w/ 
thrombotic microangiopathy, TTP, ESRD s/p failed transplant in 
___ now on ___ HD, APLS and prior DVT on warfarin, PAH, and 
seizure disorder, who presented with 1 day of nausea and 
vomiting, shoulder pain, and LLQ abdominal pain, who also 
experienced one episode of chest pain, which resolved and had 
continuing sinusitis and vulvar papules. 

============
ACUTE ISSUES
============

# Abdominal pain/constipation. Ms. ___ had evidence of 
ileus on CT abdomen/pelvis. This was deemed likely in the 
setting of poor PO intake from nausea from possible 
gastroenteritis and sinus infection. She had previously had a 
single episode of nausea/vomiting, which has now resolved. She 
was treated with an aggressive bowel regimen of senna, Colace, 
bisacodyl PO, bisacodyl PR, PEG, and lactulose. She took a 
regular diet, and nausea was treated with Zofran 4 mg q8h as 
needed. 

# ESRD, on hemodialysis MWF. ESRD ___ to thrombotic 
microangiopathy. She missed her ___ dialysis in the setting of 
being in the ED. She had no evidence of volume overload on her 
admission exam, and her electrolyte abnormalities of metabolic 
acidosis and hyperkalemia were consistent with ESRD. She 
experienced two episodes of hypotension during hemodialysis, 
where were thought most likely from fluid shifts and 
intravascular volume depletion. Her home sevelemir was 
continued. 

# Shoulder pain. This was deemed to be likely bursitis. She had 
full range of motion with no paresthesias. She had tenderness to 
palpation over deltoid/trapezius. Pain was well-controlled with 
acetaminophen and with her home pain regimen. 

# Vulvar papules. These have been long-standing for her; and she 
has experienced abscesses before. The patient will have 
outpatient GYN follow-up, and she was advised to pursue qid Siz 
baths.  

# Sinusitis. Ms. ___ had previously treated been treated 
with Bactrim and levofloxacin, however she had no drainage, and 
these were stopped. She was advised to pursue conservative 
treatment with a saline nasal spray.

==============
CHRONIC ISSUES
==============

# Vestibulopathy. Ms. ___ has chronic and long-standing 
dizziness, which she experienced before her HD session. She will 
be followed as an outpatient by her neurologist for this. 

# Antiphopholipid syndrome / Hyperfibrinolytic syndrome. She is 
on warfarin as outpatient with goal INR 1.5-2.5; managed by her 
nephrologist Dr. ___. INR was 1.6 on admission, and she was 
continued on her daily dose of 3 mg.

# Pulmonary arterial hypertension. Demonstrated on RHC in 
___. On endothelin antagonist with Opsumit with improvement 
in her symptoms and functional capacity per pulmonology. Recent 
PFTs ___ demonstrate an FVC of 1.8 liters, 70% predicted; 
FEV1 1.42 liters, 72% predicted, ratio of 79%. She did not 
receive her macitentan in house as the drug was not formulary. 
This was discussed with her outpatient pulmonologist, Dr. 
___. 

# Anemia. Chronic, normocytic anemia ___ to ESRD. She required 
no transfusions. 

# Hypertension. Previously on amlodipine and labetalol 100 mg 
bid. Currently on no anti-hypertensives, and she remained 
normotensive. 

# GERD/esophageal dysmotility. Chronic and long-standing; She 
has been worked up previously with endoscopy and has been 
treated with anti-spasmodics, but she had not been taking them 
at the time of admission. 

# Seizure disorder. Continued home lamotrigine.
